claims.text: The `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes that the cloud provider enforces independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider-level deletion-protection mechanism separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider-level deletion-protection mechanism separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (i.e., not have the `protect` option set) and still refuse to be deleted due to a cloud-provider-level deletion-protection attribute, or vice versa (protected in Pulumi but deletable at the cloud-provider level).

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/#deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself exists and documents how to distinguish Pulumi's `protect` option from cloud-provider-level deletion protection and how to resolve each.
Pulumi has no single flag to protect every resource in a stack.
Using stack transforms, you can set the `protect` option on every resource as it is registered, applying `protect: true` across the board.
The `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi itself.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes that the cloud provider or cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the provider/cloud API, separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the provider/cloud API, separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attribute are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The page 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (linked at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/#deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself) explains how to distinguish Pulumi's `protect` option from a resource's own deletion-protection attribute and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
The `retainOnDelete` resource option lets Pulumi remove a resource from state without calling the provider's delete operation, leaving the underlying cloud resource in place.
The `retainOnDelete` resource option takes the opposite approach from the `protect` resource option, which refuses to delete a resource.

A `pulumi destroy` failure can result from the resource itself being guarded against deletion rather than an engine problem, and something must remove that guard before Pulumi can delete the resource.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
An error naming a URN and mentioning `protect` indicates the Pulumi `protect` resource option is blocking deletion, resolvable per the Protect documentation.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, for example `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` or `gcp.container.Cluster`.
When a provider enforces a deletion-protection attribute, the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves independent of Pulumi, for example AWS RDS `deletionProtection`.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves independent of Pulumi, for example EC2 `disableApiTermination`.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves independent of Pulumi, for example an Azure Resource Manager management lock.
When a cloud API enforces deletion protection, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently specifies.

Setting a deletion-protection attribute to `false` only in the Pulumi program is not sufficient to allow `pulumi destroy` to succeed; a `pulumi up` must first be run so the change reaches both the live resource and Pulumi's state, and only then does `pulumi destroy` succeed.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., directly in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality, allowing `pulumi destroy` to succeed without an intervening `pulumi up`.
GCP's `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
GCP's `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
GCP's `gcp.container.Cluster` resource has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
GCP's `gcp.bigquery.Table` resource has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
GCP's `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` resource has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute, and destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless this attribute is set to `true`.
AWS's `aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` resources have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
AWS's `aws.s3.BucketV2` resource has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
AWS's `aws.ec2.Instance` resource has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
AWS's `aws.dynamodb.Table` resource has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to `false`.

Azure resources placed under a management lock (via `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`) are protected from deletion by Azure Resource Manager, and a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.

Azure's `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` resource only soft-deletes when destroyed, and recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
